blocks.text:
A free day by the ocean. The peninsula has more than 20 beaches, each with a distinct character. João Fernandes is known for its clear water and gently sloping shore, Geribá for its waves and long stretch of sand, and Ferradura for its sheltered bay and calm water.

In the evening, you can head to Rua das Pedras for restaurants and shops. Resort life comes together here: soft lighting, small shops, restaurant tables and views of the sea and hills. Options include Chez Françoise at Le Relais La Borie, Místico at the Abracadabra hotel, La Gare and Restaurante 74 at Casas Brancas.

In Búzios, the itinerary deliberately becomes more relaxed. After busy days in Rio and at Iguazu, there is no need to set off on an excursion every morning. You can choose a beach and spend a few hours there, take a boat, stroll along Rua das Pedras or spend the day at your hotel. Different sides of the peninsula offer different sea conditions: in some places the water is calm and suitable for swimming, while elsewhere the open Atlantic brings a noticeable swell.
